name: Warfarin
executiveSummary: Vitamin K antagonist. Adult: typical start **2.5–5 mg PO/day** (elderly/frail **1–2.5 mg**); adjust to INR goal (e.g. **2–3** AF/DVT; **2.5–3.5** mechanical mitral valve). Antidote: vitamin K ± PCC/FFP.
indications:
## Indications

- AF with OAC indication, DVT/PE, mechanical valves, antiphospholipid syndromes (per guideline).

## Precautions

- Many interactions (antibiotics, amiodarone, NSAIDs, alcohol, vitamin K–rich foods).
- Bleeding — educate; frequent INR at start and after changes.
- Pregnancy: teratogenic (1st trimester) — alternative anticoagulants.
- Many eligible patients move to DOACs (not mechanical valves).

> Same time daily; do not self-adjust dose.

adulto.dose: Start: **5 mg/day** × 1–2 days (or **2.5 mg** in elderly/high risk) then adjust. Usual maintenance **2–10 mg/day**. Bridge with heparin until therapeutic INR if needed.

pediatrico.dose: Start guide **0.1–0.2 mg/kg/day** (max 5–10 mg) — hematology only; frequent INR.

stability:
## Stability

- Protect from moisture/light per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bleeding, bruising; skin necrosis (rare, protein C deficiency); purple toe syndrome; teratogenicity.
